title: Supreme Court dissolves AIFF Executive Committee, appoints Committee of Administrators
summary: The Supreme Court removed Praful Patel's Executive Committee — which had stayed in office years past its constitutional term without holding elections — and appointed a 3-member Committee of Administrators (Justice A.R. Dave, S.Y. Quraishi, Bhaskar Ganguly) to run AIFF and conduct elections.

title: General Secretary Kushal Das goes on leave amid CAG audit
summary: Kushal Das, AIFF General Secretary since 2010, went on leave on health grounds after a Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) audit — examining accounts from the Praful Patel era — reportedly found multiple financial anomalies that were then being probed. AIFF has not itself published this CAG report; the finding is sourced to contemporaneous news reporting, not a document we have independently verified.
status: reported, unverified against a published primary document

title: Kushal Das resigns as General Secretary
summary: Das resigned citing health grounds, ending a 12-year tenure that news coverage describes as marred by allegations of financial improprieties (his side of it was not a matter of public record we could locate). Sunando Dhar took over as Acting General Secretary.

title: FIFA–AFC delegation visits India, sets ultimatum
summary: A joint seven-member FIFA/AFC delegation met the Committee of Administrators and issued a strict timeline for AIFF to hold elections and remove third-party (court-appointed administrator) influence, or risk suspension.

title: FIFA suspends AIFF over third-party interference
summary: FIFA suspended AIFF with immediate effect, citing "undue influence from third parties" — a breach of its statutes caused by the court-appointed Committee of Administrators running the federation instead of an elected body. India's hosting of the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup 2022 was put at risk.

title: Supreme Court orders Committee of Administrators to cease, Secretary-General to run AIFF
summary: To satisfy FIFA's core objection, the Supreme Court directed that AIFF be run by its Secretary-General on an interim basis and that the Committee of Administrators cease to exist.

sources.label: ESPN — FIFA suspends AIFF: timeline of events

title: FIFA lifts the suspension
summary: FIFA lifted AIFF's suspension after confirming the AIFF General Assembly had been reinstated and the Committee of Administrators was no longer in charge, clearing the way for elections and the U-17 Women's World Cup to proceed as hosted.

title: Kalyan Chaubey elected AIFF President
summary: Former India goalkeeper Kalyan Chaubey was elected AIFF President, defeating Bhaichung Bhutia, marking the return of an elected Executive Committee after the Committee of Administrators period.

sources.label: ESPN — AIFF elections: Kalyan Chaubey elected president

title: AIFF's own legal head publicly accuses President Chaubey of corruption
summary: Nilanjan Bhattacharjee, then AIFF's principal legal advisor, alleged in a letter to the Prime Minister that Chaubey created "corruption avenues" through non-transparent tender processes and preferential allotment — including broadcasting tenders for I-League, IWL and the Santosh Trophy allegedly steered to a company close to the president — and alleged attempts to siphon federation funds for personal use. This is a disputed allegation, not an established finding.

title: AIFF terminates the legal head who made the allegations
summary: AIFF terminated Bhattacharjee's position as principal legal advisor shortly after he made the corruption allegations against Chaubey public.

title: Chaubey serves legal notice on Bhattacharjee, calls allegations baseless
summary: President Chaubey served a legal notice on Bhattacharjee over the corruption allegations, calling them baseless and aimed at damaging his reputation. We found no public report of the notice or the underlying allegations having since been adjudicated by a court.
status: denied by Chaubey — outcome not publicly established

title: AIFF constitution / election-timing case before the Supreme Court (Rahul Mehra matter)
summary: A long-running case over AIFF's constitution and whether the Executive Committee elected in September 2022 is entitled to a full four-year term has been before the Supreme Court, with hearings concluded and judgment reserved as of the sources below. Some stakeholders argue the court could order fresh elections.

title: FSDL puts the 2025-26 Indian Super League season "on hold"
summary: Football Sports Development Limited (FSDL) — AIFF's commercial partner for the ISL since 2010 — put the 2025-26 season on hold, citing unresolved terms for renewing the Master Rights Agreement (MRA) with AIFF, which was due to expire 8 December 2025. This directly affected the livelihoods of ISL clubs, players and staff.

title: President Chaubey: "We are going through a crisis for which we are not responsible"
summary: With the ISL in limbo and no commercial partner secured, Chaubey publicly stated AIFF was not responsible for the crisis, while asserting the federation's stability amid what multiple outlets described as ongoing uncertainty in Indian football.

title: Top-tier league still "in limbo" months later
summary: By mid-November 2025, explainer coverage described Indian football's top-tier league as still without a resolved commercial framework, months after the season was meant to start.

title: Sports Minister announces ISL 2026 restart under a new financial model
summary: Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya announced the delayed ISL would start 14 February 2026, after the FSDL Master Rights Agreement lapsed. Reporting describes a new central-pool budget of roughly Rs 24.26 crore replacing the FSDL commercial arrangement, with clubs paying a reduced ~Rs 1 crore participation fee — a materially different financial structure for the league AIFF governs.
